theme.title: Five on the Floor
theme.subtitle: Teams, stars and stories from across basketball
theme.recap: The best numbers come from all over basketball history. Which answer surprised you most?

questions.prompt: What was Reggie Miller's career high in points?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: he scored a career-high 57 points against the Charlotte Hornets in a 134–122 win

funFacts.text: Pacers fans booed the draft selection that brought Miller to Indiana; they had wanted hometown favorite Steve Alford.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: fans watching the 1987 NBA draft booed Pacers President Donnie Walsh for the selection

funFacts.text: Miller became the Pacers' primary scoring option after Indiana traded Chuck Person in the offseason.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: After Chuck Person was traded from the Pacers during the 1992 offseason

funFacts.text: Years later, Jermaine O'Neal stopped scoring late in a big night rather than surpass his veteran teammate's franchise mark.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: left the game with 1:43 remaining to preserve Miller's 57-point record

questions.prompt: What was Steve Nash's assists-per-game average for the 2004–05 Suns?
questions.note: 11.5 assists each night in his first MVP season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Nash finished the season averaging 11.5 assists per game

funFacts.text: Nash shot 50.2% from the field and 43.1% from three during the regular season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: while making 50.2% of his field goals and 43.1% of his three-pointers

funFacts.text: Nash won MVP while Mike D'Antoni took Coach of the Year and Bryan Colangelo Executive of the Year.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: He ended up winning the MVP award. D'Antoni was awarded Coach of the Year

funFacts.text: Quentin Richardson won the Three-Point Shootout during the same season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Quentin Richardson won the Three-Point Shootout

questions.prompt: Golden State set an NBA record for consecutive regular-season home wins. How long was the streak?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Warriors also set an NBA record 54-straight regular-season home-game winning streak,

funFacts.text: The home winning streak stretched across two seasons, beginning in January 2015.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: which spanned from January 31, 2015, to March 29, 2016

funFacts.text: Boston ended Golden State's long run at Oracle Arena with a narrow April road win.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Golden State lost at home for the first time since January 27, 2015. They fell to the Boston Celtics

funFacts.text: Before Golden State broke it, Chicago's 1990s dynasty had held the home-win-streak record.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The previous record of 44 was held by the 1995–96 Chicago Bulls

questions.prompt: After an offensive rebound, what is the NBA shot clock reset to?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The shot clock is instead set to 14 following an offensive rebound.

funFacts.text: FIBA introduced the shorter offensive-rebound clock years before the NBA adopted it.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: FIBA adopted this in 2014 and the NBA adopted in 2018

funFacts.text: A defender merely tipping the ball does not restart the clock if the offense keeps possession.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The shot clock does not reset if a defender makes short contact with the ball

funFacts.text: Missing the rim entirely on an airball also leaves the previous countdown running.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: or if a shot attempt misses the rim entirely and airballs

questions.prompt: On March 25, 2016, the Warriors and Mavericks set a record for combined threes in a game. How many?
questions.note: 39: 21 by Golden State, 18 by Dallas. A record at the time.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: both teams combined for 39 made three-pointers (21 by the Warriors, 18 by the Mavericks), an all-time NBA record,

funFacts.text: Golden State became the first NBA team to sink a thousand three-pointers in a single regular season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the first team in league history to hit 1,000 three-pointers in a single season

funFacts.text: Assistant coach Luke Walton ran the Warriors early in the year while Steve Kerr recovered from back trouble.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: assistant coach Luke Walton coaching for the team after it was confirmed that coach Steve Kerr's back would not heal

funFacts.text: Draymond Green recorded a rare five-by-five stat line during an overtime trip to Boston.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Draymond Green recorded a five-by-five game
